annotations.text:
THE SHELL — these are one app, not seven pages
Every artboard carries the same 72px rail: Map, Quests, Defend, Boss, Party, Journal, Console. The active item is lit; badges carry live counts (4 invasions at the border, 2 sign-offs waiting), so the rail is the notification surface as well as the navigation.

The session loop runs Defend (repel invasions) -> Map (choose) -> Quests (build) -> Journal (write). Boss, Party and Console are entered from the rail whenever, not in sequence.

DENOMINATORS (§5.1a)
The tilde in "3 of ~5" is load-bearing, not decoration. Tier 3 is still being authored, so the total is an estimate and the UI says so. Content carries the fact (authoring: partial); this screen decides it renders as a tilde.

MEDALS AND DATAMINE (§5.10, §5.5)
Unearned medal slots render greyed but present — visible-but-locked, same psychology as the skill tree.

Submit actually reads the editor. The starter indexes inventory[block] directly, so a missing block raises KeyError instead of answering False. It fails until you fix it — .get(), or a membership check. Two failures open the Datamine.

THE INVASION LADDER — needs your ruling
The spec names a review interval and never specifies it. Proposed: an invasion arrives at 1, 3, 7, 16, then 35 days untouched. Repel one and it stays away longer; miss it and it returns a rung sooner rather than from zero, because resetting punishes a bad night and floods the next border.

SCARS (§5.3, §3.5)
Failed attempts are listed with what actually went wrong, newest first, and never collapsed behind a toggle. Four attempts on a boss is not a bad record — it is the record.

THE DC WARNING LIVES HERE, NOT IN THE ENGINE (§5.1)
The engine returns 20. This layer decides that 20 earns a triangle. Every other surface reads the same number and renders it its own way, so no two can disagree.

STILL OPEN: THE +0 XP MEDAL
At base DC 5 the clamp absorbs both negative modifiers, so a medal can legitimately pay nothing. Not solved on these boards — it needs a rendering that explains itself before it ships.

LEXICON RESET — 2026-08-27
Patrol → Invasion, Muster → Defend, Chronicle → Journal, Board → Party, Quest → Quests in the rail.

Two reasons. The old words were ones an 11-year-old meets in late teens at best; and "Board" collided with "quest board" when quest was already in the lexicon. Party won over Levels because the curriculum already numbers Tiers 0–7, and level (from XP) is a different number than tier (from position) — putting both on screen invites exactly one question with a confusing answer.

Renamed everywhere, not only here: spec, content schema (kind: invasion), engine XP kinds, curriculum. Boss 7 puts him inside the engine repo reading that YAML, so the authoring words and the playing words have to be the same words.
